steps.body: Pair the counters into twos. If every counter finds a partner, the number is even; one left standing alone makes it odd.
steps.narration: Pair the counters into twos. If every counter finds a partner, the number is even; one left standing alone makes it odd.

widget.prompt: Pair up 14 counters. Odd or even?
widget.oddFeedback: 14 pairs up completely (7 pairs, 0 left). No leftover means even.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 14 makes 7 pairs with none left over.

predict.prompt: Pair up 14 counters. Will one be left over?
predict.reveal: 14 makes 7 full pairs; nothing is left standing, so 14 is even. Try 15 and one counter stands alone — that leftover is what makes a number odd.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2a pairs.
invariants: Rearranging counters into pairs, rows, or columns changes the VIEW of a quantity, never its count — the model and the total must agree for g2a pairs.
misconceptions: Believing a taller or wider arrangement holds more, or that a leftover counter can be ignored when judging parity.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What single change to the arrangement would change what the number IS, not just how it looks?
